records.sourceName: Alaska Legislature: AS 15.15.010-15.15.470 (voting and counting)
limitations: Tabulation order and timing of rounds are not stated in what was retrieved
records.summary: General elections are conducted by ranked-choice voting: each ballot is first tabulated for its highest-ranked continuing candidate, and tabulation proceeds in rounds unless a candidate has more than half of active ballots

records.sourceName: Alaska Legislature: AS 15.20 absentee voting
limitations: State law says when review and counting may happen; it does not say when or how the Division of Elections publishes the results of that count
records.notes: Evidence anchor: "On the second day following the day of the election, the election supervisor"
records.summary: Alaska questioned ballots are reviewed by the election supervisor beginning on the second day after the election, and counting of questioned ballots that pass review begins on the third day.

records.sourceName: Alaska Legislature: AS 15.20 absentee voting
limitations: Describes where late-arriving absentee ballots go; the date and form of the resulting count are not stated
records.notes: Evidence anchor: "after the completion of the district absentee ballot counting review shall be forwarded immediately to the director"
records.summary: Absentee ballots that reach an election supervisor after the district absentee ballot counting review is complete are forwarded to the director rather than counted in that district review, so they arrive as a later batch.

records.sourceName: Arizona Legislature: A.R.S. 16-551
limitations: Arizona 'early ballots' are mail ballots, including those dropped off in person; the statute does not separate them
records.notes: Evidence anchor: "before 7:00 p.m. on election day"
records.summary: Arizona early ballots received before 7:00 p.m. on Election Day go to the early election board for counting.

records.sourceName: Arizona Legislature: A.R.S. 16-551
limitations: A restriction on releasing early-ballot tallies, not a schedule; it sets the earliest point, not when counties publish
records.notes: Evidence anchor: "one hour after the closing of the polls on election day, whichever occurs first"
records.summary: Partial or complete tallies of the early election board may not be released before all precincts have reported or one hour after polls close on Election Day, whichever occurs first.

records.sourceName: Arizona Legislature: A.R.S. 16-622
limitations: Permission to release unofficial returns, not a schedule or an order between methods
records.notes: Evidence anchor: "unofficial returns may be released during the counting of the ballots by vote tabulating equipment"
records.summary: After the polls close, unofficial returns may be released during counting of ballots by vote tabulating equipment, subject to the early-ballot restrictions in 16-550 and 16-551.

records.sourceName: Arizona Legislature: A.R.S. 16-550
limitations: A cure deadline: it shows ballots can still be added, not how many or how they lean
records.notes: Evidence anchor: "not later than the fifth business day after a primary, general or special election that includes a federal office"
records.summary: Arizona voters may correct a missing early-ballot signature until the fifth business day after a general election that includes a federal office, so ballots can still be added after Election Day.

records.sourceName: Public.Law (mirror of C.R.S.): C.R.S. 1-7.5-107.5
limitations: Read from a public mirror of the statute (secondary)
The section sits in the mail-ballot-election article; its application to a state general election is not confirmed from this page alone
records.notes: Evidence anchor: "fifteen days prior to the election"
records.summary: Counting of Colorado mail ballots may begin fifteen days before the election, and counties with more than ten thousand active electors at the previous general election must begin no later than four days before.

records.sourceName: Public.Law (mirror of C.R.S.): C.R.S. 1-7.5-107.5
limitations: Read from a public mirror of the statute (secondary)
A restriction, not a release schedule
records.notes: Evidence anchor: "until after 7 p.m. on election day"
records.summary: No information concerning the mail-ballot count may be released by election officials or watchers until after 7:00 p.m. on Election Day.

records.sourceName: Florida Legislature: Fla. Stat. 102.141
limitations: A deadline for reporting to the Department of State, not a statement of when a county posts publicly
Early and vote-by-mail are reported together, so the first batch is a mixed batch the statute does not separate
records.notes: Evidence anchor: "within 30 minutes after the polls close"
records.summary: Each Florida county must report early voting and tabulated vote-by-mail results to the Department of State within 30 minutes after polls close, and then update at least every 45 minutes until all results are reported.

records.sourceName: Florida Legislature: Fla. Stat. 102.141
limitations: A restriction, not a schedule
records.notes: Evidence anchor: "before the close of the polls on election day"
records.summary: Florida bars making public the tabulation of votes cast in the pre-Election-Day processing of early voting and vote-by-mail ballots (ss. 101.5614(8), 101.657, 101.68(2)) before the close of the polls on Election Day.

records.sourceName: Florida Legislature: Fla. Stat. 101.68
limitations: A cure deadline: it shows ballots can still be added, not how many or how they lean
records.notes: Evidence anchor: "5 p.m. on the 2nd day after the election"
records.summary: A Florida vote-by-mail voter may cure a missing or mismatched signature until 5 p.m. on the second day after the election.

records.sourceName: Georgia.gov: Georgia general election 2026
limitations: Voter-facing summary page; the statute was not retrieved
Says nothing about when absentee ballots are counted or published
records.notes: Evidence anchor: "by the time polls close at 7 p.m."
records.summary: Georgia voters can return a completed absentee ballot to a drop box or the county registrar's office until polls close at 7 p.m.

records.sourceName: Iowa Legislature: Iowa Code 53.23
limitations: A staffing standard, not a guarantee of when results post
records.notes: Evidence anchor: "complete the counting of absentee ballots by 10:00 p.m. on election day"
records.summary: Iowa's special precinct election board must have enough members to finish counting absentee ballots by 10:00 p.m. on Election Day.

records.sourceName: Iowa Legislature: Iowa Code 53.23
limitations: A restriction on the board's own tabulation; it does not say when the county publishes the count
records.notes: Evidence anchor: "until the count is completed on election day"
records.summary: Where the Iowa special precinct election board begins counting absentee ballots the day before Election Day, it may not release its tabulation until the count is completed on Election Day.

records.sourceName: Kansas Revisor of Statutes: K.S.A. 25-1134
limitations: Advance voting combines mail and in-person advance ballots; the statute does not separate them
records.notes: Evidence anchor: "shall not complete final tabulation prior to election day"
records.summary: Kansas advance voting ballots (mail and in-person advance voting together) may have their original canvass before Election Day, but final tabulation may not be completed before Election Day.

records.sourceName: Kansas Revisor of Statutes: K.S.A. 25-3104
limitations: County canvass date; the state certification date is separate
records.notes: Evidence anchor: "not later than 13 days following any election"
records.summary: The Kansas county canvass is held on the Monday after the election, and a county may move it to a business day no later than 13 days after the election.

records.sourceName: Maine Legislature: 21-A M.R.S. 759
limitations: Read from the statute text as retrieved; a restriction, not a schedule
records.notes: Evidence anchor: "until after the polls have closed on election day"
records.summary: Maine absentee ballots may not be counted, and results may not be obtained or released, until after the polls have closed on Election Day.

records.sourceName: Nebraska Legislature: Neb. Rev. Stat. 32-1027
limitations: Processing window only; Nebraska results are released after polls close in practice, which this source does not say
records.notes: Evidence anchor: "not earlier than the second Friday before the election"
records.summary: The Nebraska counting board may begin its duties no earlier than the second Friday before the election.

records.sourceName: Nebraska Legislature: Neb. Rev. Stat. 32-1027
limitations: A tabulation window; it does not say when the count is published
records.notes: Evidence anchor: "twenty-four hours prior to the opening of the polls"
records.summary: Nebraska counting boards may begin counting early ballots no earlier than 24 hours before polls open on Election Day.

records.sourceName: Public.Law (mirror of N.Y. Election Law): N.Y. Election Law 9-209

Processing rule only

records.summary: New York boards of canvassers examine absentee and mail ballot affirmation envelopes within one day of receipt, so mail ballots are processed on a rolling basis.

limitations: Read from a public mirror of the statute (secondary)
A cure rule: it does not say how many ballots are affected
records.notes: Evidence anchor: "within one day of such determination"
records.summary: New York boards notify a voter of a ballot-envelope defect within one day of determining it, and the voter may cure; ballots can be added after Election Day.

records.notes: Evidence anchor: "shall not tabulate or count the votes on those ballots before that time"

records.sourceName: Ohio Laws and Administrative Rules: R.C. 3505.183
limitations: Describes the holding of provisional ballots; the date of the count is not stated here
records.notes: Evidence anchor: "until the validity of those ballots is determined"
records.summary: Ohio provisional ballot envelopes are kept sealed in a secure location until their validity is determined, so provisional ballots are counted after Election Day review.

records.sourceName: South Carolina Legislature: S.C. Code Title 7 Chapter 15 (absentee voting)
limitations: Processing window only
records.notes: Evidence anchor: "Beginning no earlier than 7:00 a.m. on the second day immediately preceding election day"
records.summary: South Carolina managers may begin examining absentee ballot envelopes no earlier than 7:00 a.m. on the second day before Election Day.

records.sourceName: South Carolina Legislature: S.C. Code Title 7 Chapter 15 (absentee voting)
limitations: A tabulation window; it does not say when the count is published
records.notes: Evidence anchor: "Beginning no earlier than 7:00 a.m. on election day"
records.summary: South Carolina absentee ballots may be tabulated beginning no earlier than 7:00 a.m. on Election Day, including absentee ballots received on Election Day.

records.sourceName: South Carolina Legislature: S.C. Code Title 7 Chapter 15 (absentee voting)
limitations: States the unit; whether a county publishes it separately is not stated
records.notes: Evidence anchor: "is responsible for the tabulation and reporting of ballots at the absentee voting precinct"
records.summary: Each South Carolina county board is responsible for tabulating and reporting the ballots of an absentee voting precinct, so absentee results form their own reporting unit.

records.sourceName: South Carolina Legislature: S.C. Code Title 7 Chapter 15 (absentee voting)
limitations: Means no late-arriving mail ballots for ordinary absentee voters; military and overseas voters are covered by a separate rule
records.notes: Evidence anchor: "after time for closing of the polls"
records.summary: South Carolina does not count an absentee ballot received by the election officials after the time for closing of the polls.

limitations: Describes a later processing meeting; its date is not stated
